newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian lawmakers charged in kidnap-murder case.
newsitem.headline: Colombian lawmakers charged in kidnap-murder case.

text.p: Three politicians from Colombia's southern Caqueta province have been arrested in connection with the abduction of a former ruling party legislator who was found dead in May, authorities said on Friday.

A senior police official in the province identified the suspects as Pablo Adriano Munoz Parra and Andres Paez Moreno, both of the ruling Liberal Party, and Boris Alberto Cabrera of the leftist Patriotic Union party. All three are members of the the Caqueta provincial congress.

The police official, Col. Jose Orlando Cabrera, said a team of judicial policemen from Bogota had flown to Florencia, the capital of Caqueta, to make the arrests on Thursday after warrants were issued. "If warrants were issued for these people it's because they were involved in some way," he said, referring to the kidnapping and subsequent death of former Liberal Party legislator Rodrigo Turbay.

Turbay, 37, a former president of the lower house of Congress, was abducted by Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas in June 1995 and accused of stealing funds from the local government. In a statement sent to a radio station in Caqueta, the FARC said he drowned on May 3 when the boat in which rebels were moving him from one hideout to another capsized.

Turbay, who was from an influential family of Caqueta politicians, had been stripped of his Liberal Party seat in Congress shortly before his kidnapping because of his alleged links to known drug traffickers.
His mother, Ines Cote, has charged that Adriano Munoz, a leading candidate for the Caqueta governorship, paid off the FARC to ensure that Turbay would not be released.
